title: Probability and Conditional Probability
purpose: Seed probability semantics and conditional reasoning so Lantern can reason about uncertainty, base rates, independence and evidence updates without confusing conditional directions or treating probability as truth.

concepts.definition: A number from 0 to 1 assigned under a declared probabilistic model to represent uncertainty or relative frequency/degree of belief as specified.
The declared set of possible outcomes considered by a probability model.
A subset of the sample space whose probability may be evaluated.
NOT A contains outcomes in the sample space that are not in A.
P(A AND B), the probability that both events occur.
P(A|B), probability of A under the condition that B is established, defined when P(B)>0.
The unconditional probability of an event after accounting for relevant alternatives/variables in the model.
Prior/background prevalence or probability of an event in the relevant population before case-specific evidence.
A and B are independent under a model when learning one does not change the probability of the other; equivalently P(A AND B)=P(A)P(B) where defined.
A and B may be independent given C even when not marginally independent.
A and B cannot both occur, so P(A AND B)=0; this is not the same as independence.
How compatible observed evidence is with a hypothesis/model, often represented by P(E|H); not the same as P(H|E).
Probability assigned before incorporating the currently considered evidence.
Probability after updating a prior with evidence under a specified model.
P(H|E)=P(E|H)P(H)/P(E) when terms are defined and P(E)>0.
Probability of an event can be decomposed over a mutually exclusive/exhaustive partition.
Probability-weighted average value under a declared distribution; not a guaranteed outcome.

guards.reason: Conditional probability is directional; posterior requires base rate and evidence probability.
A high likelihood does not imply a high posterior when H is rare or E common under alternatives.
Nontrivial mutually exclusive events are dependent.
Zero probability can be model-relative and does not establish impossibility outside the model.
Probability one is model-relative and may not equal logical necessity or universal truth.
Expected value summarizes a distribution and need not be an attainable or next outcome.
Lack of detected correlation does not establish probabilistic independence.
Probability cannot grant permission or authority.

invariants: Every numerical probability is interpreted relative to a declared or recoverable model, population/sample space and scope.
Conditional probability is directional: P(A|B) and P(B|A) are generally different.
Base rates matter when updating hypotheses from evidence.
Independence and mutual exclusivity are distinct.
Probability zero/one under a model is not automatically metaphysical impossibility/logical necessity.
Expected value is not a guaranteed outcome.
Probability describes uncertainty under a model; it is not identical to truth, confidence, source quality or authority.
Empirical probability estimates require methodology to justify population generalization.
Arithmetic should be delegated to deterministic quantitative computation where available; seed rules define semantics and selection constraints.

provenance.authoring_basis: Kolmogorov-style elementary probability, conditional probability and Bayesian updating foundations adapted to Lantern's bounded epistemic reasoning.
